$comment: Ghar ki Hawa's indoor model defaults (P3), read by indoorDefaults.ts. Every value carries its source. Hours are India time; an end past 24 runs into the next morning.

closed.source: Saans plan values for a home with windows shut; in line with the air exchange, penetration and infiltration ranges reviewed in Chen & Zhao (2011), Atmos. Environ. 45:275–288.

ajar.source: Saans plan values for one open window (single-sided ventilation).

open.source: Saans plan values for two or more open windows (cross-ventilation); with the windows open, outside air comes straight in, so nothing is filtered out.

deposition_per_h.source: PM2.5 settling onto indoor surfaces; Saans plan value, in line with Chen & Zhao (2011).

cooking.hours_source: Assumed meal times: breakfast, lunch and dinner, an hour each.

electric.source: No combustion. Frying still makes some smoke, which this leaves out.

lpg.source: WHO Indoor Air Quality Guidelines: Household Fuel Combustion (2014) set 0.23 mg/min as the unvented emission rate target, which gas burners are taken to meet; we use the target itself as an upper bound.

png.source: As LPG: piped natural gas burns as cleanly (WHO 2014 lists both as clean fuels).

kerosene.source: Estimate. WHO (2014) interim target for unvented stoves, 1.75 mg/min; WHO advises against kerosene, and wick stoves can exceed this.

biomass.source: Estimate. Real-world chulha emission factor about 10.5 g PM2.5 per kg of wood (Atmos. Chem. Phys. 18, 15169, 2018); we assume about 1 kg burnt an hour and that about 3% of the smoke stays in the home's air rather than leaving through the kitchen's openings. Needs checking against kitchen measurements.

smoker.source: Marlboro cigarettes emitted 2.2 mg PM2.5 a minute under a fixed puffing protocol ("Measuring indoor fine particle concentrations, emission rates, and decay rates from cannabis use in a residence", Atmos. Environ. X, 2021); a cigarette lasts about 10 minutes. We assume one cigarette an hour while awake.

incense.source: About 7 µg/s (25 mg/h) per stick, measured in a closed room (Int. J. Environ. Res. Public Health 20:587, 2022); chamber studies find more. Assumed one stick, morning and evening.

mosquito_coil.source: Liu et al. (2003), Environ. Health Perspect. 111:1454–1460: four coil brands emitted 63–117 mg/h, one coil about 75–137 cigarettes' worth. We use 85 mg/h, burning from 21:00 to 05:00.

purifier.source: When the home has no purifier, the plan suggests one with a CADR of 5 room volumes an hour: AHAM's sizing rule (CADR in cfm at least two-thirds of the floor area in ft²) works out to 5 air changes an hour under an 8 ft (2.4 m) ceiling.
